title: Lady Snowblood
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A 1970s adult gekiga set in Meiji-era Japan (the 1890s). Yuki, born in prison to Sayo, whose husband and son were murdered and who was raped by a gang of four criminals, is raised as an assassin sworn to avenge her family (ANN House of 1000 Manga; Dark Horse blurb). Episodic stories move through brothels, the underworld and Westernizing high society.
life_message: A life inherited as a single purpose of vengeance; the story presents retribution as total and unquestioned.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yuki is 'sworn to revenge since the day she was born' (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Operates outside law as paid assassin among outlaws (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Avenging Sayo and her murdered husband and son drives everything (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Allies with beggars and prostitutes, attacks elites (ANN).

folkways.japan: Rooted in the Japanese vendetta (katakiuchi) tradition and 1970s gekiga, set against Meiji-era debates over Westernization.

delivery.evidence: ANN: Koike plays to nationalistic sentiments; Westernizing extremes are assassination targets.

personified.character: Westernizing officials and intellectuals (proposals such as Arinori Mori's, per ANN)

delivery.note: Revenge is never questioned, and modernizers appear chiefly as extreme proposals that become targets.

winners_losers: Yuki and her quest win sympathy; the gang and Westernizing elites lose. The reviewer notes women other than Yuki often suffer abuse in Koike's work.
to_verify: Whether the Westernizers are drawn as strawmen; ANN supports 'extremes' but not a clear Strawman call.
